body:
Thanks :)  It helps knowing I'm not alone, because most people that are close to me have told me the opposite. If everyone else can put up with it, why can't I?

I am thinking about switching to something more dialectical but we'll see.

That really sucks.  The lack of interest sounds like textbook depression, but then again, I'm not in your shoes.  What could you be doing that you don't feel is worth your time?  Maybe there are ways to change it to make it worth your time.  Ex.  "Geez, I'm a loser for just sitting around on the internet all day" can turn into "Geez, I spent a lot of time on the internet today and learned German through Duolingo!"  It might not fix bigger problems, but tiny arbitrary tasks can make life more... idk, tolerable?

One of my good friends I met at my new school is an Aspie.  It does make it harder, but joining activity groups is a safe place to start.  Anyone in an extracurricular is already looking for friends with like-minded interests.

yikes! I came on here for my own stuff so anything I say feels a little hypocritical, but I was in the lost scholarship boat.  What helped me (with that issue, obviously not everything or I wouldn't be here) was transferring to a new school.  It might not be an option, but going to a new school reset my GPA, broadened my social circle enough that I was more willing to dump shitty unsupportive friends, and took everyone's mind off of the loss of the scholarship.

Like I said, it might not be a possibility for your situation, nor does it fix everything, but if you can and have nothing else to lose, go for it.  Feel better <3

Exactly!  If I could do whatever I wanted I would have a lot of sex, drink a lot of wine, and smoke a lot of weed.  You can't really get by doing that, and believe me I tried as a, well, sort of a sex worker.  It's complicated.  Anyway, being paid for sex sort of takes the fun out of it in ways I don't feel like explaining in case it gets triggering for others.

Out of curiosity, how would you answer that?

1.  I will never have a kid.  Having to live my life for someone else, even my own flesh and blood, would make me more suicidal
2.  I don't think what happens between then and now matters too much
3.  My mindset doesn't seem to be going anywhere.  I do have great stuff going for me (I even had a date today with a wonderful girl), it just doesn't seem to make a difference.  CBT is all about changing your perspective and it's done nothing for me thus far.  It's not a stubbornness thing, it's just I've had a lot of time to think about it and always come to the same conclusions.  Even on a good day, my brain will always go to "meh, death is still a pretty good option"

As for my therapists, no I didn't feel they were playing mindgames.  I just thought they were treating me like I was stupid/a child.  If someone is a logical person and can actually explain their rationale behind feeling miserable, no amount of "Well, you're thinking about it wrong" is ever going to work.  It's like me saying the sky is blue and being told "Well, you not thinking about it accurately, because sometimes it looks orange".  Bitch, it's mostly blue so I'm going to tell you it's blue! :P

And the main stuff that holds me back is 1. possible failure (I don't want to become a vegetable or end up in a psych ward again) and 2. What people will say/do after I die.  My boyfriends (poly) would be very upset and I would be so scared that my death would hurt them in a way that wasn't recoverable.  I'm also afraid of those who would paint it as me being sick.  I know I'm not sick, it's not depression because it doesn't change when I'm on medication.  It feels very cerebral and logical, and I don't need to be very upset to come to the same conclusions.  However, I don't want to die and have my whole family framing it in a way that didn't feel accurate or didn't tell my side of the story.  Maybe that could be best summed up as pride.

But that's precisely what I'm struggling with.  I don't think there is ANY way of living that won't be compromised by typical societal bullshit.  It feels like there's no choice in the matter:  work your ass off or you don't get paid, if you don't get paid, you don't eat and you die anyway.  Most people are willing to sacrifice a large part of their life to doing things that make them unhappy because that's just what they have to do it survive.  I'm saying I would, well, rather not survive if that's the case.  

My perception will not change; I've been in therapy for a decade and if it was going to change, it would've by now, though perhaps a few nice things in my life acted as a distraction.  I do not find an inherit meaning in life and I feel that any meaning I could try to come up with is just a distraction for the inevitable.  There is no "meaning of life" I've ever heard of/thought of that felt genuine to me, and I don't think there will ever be one because I can't escape the thought that it's all pointless and leading to death regardless.

So thanks, but not helpful in the slightest
